alternatives.transcript: A place in a group doesn't guarantee a turn. For teachers planning a practical workshop, every hand makes that missing turn visible, then helps make room for it. This fictional lesson has 28 learners, three microscopes, and thirty minutes. Each learner needs four full minutes, including reset. Only 21 complete turns fit. Zara is one of seven learners without a turn. Compare ways to make room. Keep the equipment and add ten minutes, or keep the finish time and add one microscope. Neither choice shortens anyone's turn. If extra equipment isn't available, lock it. The time option remains. Unlock it and preview the extra place instead. Now Zara has a real slot, minute twenty four to twenty eight at place four. This is still a preview. The current plan hasn't changed. Apply it. 28 learners now have complete turns. The room is driven by those scheduled slots. Select a learner to see their time and place. But workshops change. At minute eight, one microscope stops working. Every hand preserves the eight completed turns and rebuilds what comes next. The remaining plan serves 23. Five learners still need a full turn. The shortage is visible again, without erasing the work already done. Compare recovery. This time, six extra minutes are enough. The planner carries forward the completed turns and uses the three remaining places. Apply the thirty six minute plan. All 28 have complete paths again. Zara's turn is now minute thirty two to thirty six at place two. Earlier completed turns keep their original times and places. The recovery changes the future schedule while preserving the past, and every scheduled turn still lasts the full four minutes. Open the facilitator kit. The real run sheet lists every scheduled learner, activity, time, and place. Zara's row matches the recovered plan. Individual cards carry the same schedule, while any missing turns are marked explicitly. This is a local proof of concept with public source and planning documents. It plans opportunities. It doesn't measure attendance or learning. Every hand. Make room for every learner's hands on turn.
